Motorola Boosts Counter-Drone Security Footprint With D-Fend Buyout
Motorola Solutions, Inc. MSI has augmented its presence in the rapidly expanding counter-drone security market with the acquisition of D-Fend Solutions. The transaction adds D-Fend's field-proven counter-unmanned aerial systems (C-UAS) technology to Motorola's broader mission-critical safety and security ecosystem.
The $1.5-billion deal appears to be the call of the hour as unauthorized drones increasingly pose security risks to airports, stadiums, critical infrastructure, military installations and densely populated areas. In addition to securing another fast-growing business, D-Fend expands Motorola's addressable market, enabling it to leverage extensive public-safety customer relationships to accelerate adoption of counter-drone technology.
D-Fend Strengthens Counter-Drone Capabilities
The D-Fend acquisition is expected to strengthen Motorola's presence in the fast-growing counter-drone market. D-Fend's EnforceAir platform differentiates itself from conventional systems that typically rely on jamming or kinetic interception, which can disrupt nearby communications or pose collateral risks.
EnforceAir uses radio-frequency cyber-takeover technology to detect and assume control of unauthorized drones and safely redirect them to a designated landing area. Importantly, the platform can neutralize rogue drones without affecting authorized drone operations or surrounding communications infrastructure. This makes the solution well suited for sensitive environments such as airports, large public events, urban areas and other locations where jamming or kinetic methods may be less practical.
Acquisition Bolsters Broader Drone Strategy
The buyout also complements Motorola's expanding presence across the unmanned-systems ecosystem. Through Silvus Technologies, the company already offers resilient wireless networking solutions used in defense applications, including unmanned platforms. Its partnership with BRINC further provides public-safety agencies with drones-as-first-responders capabilities, enabling aerial situational awareness and real-time video transmission to command centers.
The addition of D-Fend broadens Motorola's exposure across defense-focused unmanned communications, public-safety drone applications and counter-drone solutions. Moreover, the company's established relationships with federal agencies, state and local public-safety organizations and enterprise customers could provide a ready distribution channel for D-Fend's offerings.
Management noted that Motorola has worked with D-Fend for several years and jointly pursued opportunities with federal law-enforcement agencies prior to the transaction. The combination of complementary technologies and an established customer network could support D-Fend's growth without requiring Motorola to build a separate go-to-market infrastructure.
Despite the $1.5-billion purchase price and related financing costs, management expects the transaction to be modestly accretive to earnings in 2027. D-Fend's existing profitability, healthy growth trajectory and expanding addressable market are likely to support the expected contribution.
The buyout could eventually produce a more comprehensive air-to-ground security platform, offering a product breadth that may become increasingly important as public-safety customers look to consolidate security workflows rather than deploy isolated point solutions. It could further help Motorola better compete with rivals such as Ondas Inc. ONDS, Unusual Machines, Inc. UMAC and Draganfly Inc. DPRO.

Young America Capital Advises DeepNeuronic on Sale to Motorola Solutions
Tue, September 29, 2026 at 8:22 AM PDT 2 min read
Covilhã-based AI video analytics company to be integrated into Motorola Solutions' Avigilon platform
MAMARONECK, N.Y., Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Young America Capital, LLC ("YAC") today announced that it advised DeepNeuronic, a Portuguese developer of AI video analytics, on its sale to Motorola Solutions, Inc. (NYSE: MSI). Motorola Solutions acquired 100% of DeepNeuronic's share capital, including its Brazilian subsidiary. Terms were not disclosed.
DeepNeuronic was founded in 2021 by Vasco Lopes and Bruno Degardin, who met at Portugal's University of Beira Interior and earned their PhDs there in artificial intelligence and computer vision. Their software reads live camera feeds and flags incidents as they happen. Highway operators, airports, manufacturers and retailers in Portugal and Brazil already run it on the cameras they have. Motorola Solutions will build the technology into Avigilon, its video security platform, which serves customers in more than 100 countries. DeepNeuronic's 17-person team is joining Motorola Solutions and will stay in Covilhã.
"This was one of the sharper deals we worked on this year," said Peter Formanek, Founder and CEO of YAC. "Vasco and Bruno had a product customers were already paying for and a clear view of where video analytics was going. Motorola Solutions saw it too. Our job was to get both sides to a deal that worked, across two continents and a lot of time zones, and Ran did exactly that."
Ran Zfoni, Vice President and Head of Israel & Europe Tech at YAC, advised DeepNeuronic's founders through the transaction. Cuatrecasas served as legal counsel to DeepNeuronic, with a team led by partner Vasco Bivar de Azevedo.
"The founders knew what they wanted: a buyer that could scale the technology and would keep the team together in Covilhã," said Zfoni. "Motorola Solutions was that buyer. Congratulations to Vasco, Bruno and everyone at DeepNeuronic."
Young America Capital, LLC is an investment bank based in Mamaroneck, New York. YAC advises founders and owners of lower-middle-market companies in the U.S. and abroad on M&A, capital raising and strategic transactions. Member FINRA/SIPC. www.yacapital.com

Motorolans on a Mission: Serving the Community From the Office to the Front Lines
Tue, September 29, 2026 at 6:35 AM PDT 3 min read
NORTHAMPTON, MA / ACCESS Newswire / September 29, 2026 / While most people use their vacation to disconnect, U.K.-based Motorola Solutions employee Mike Beddoes dedicates his time to answering a higher call, stepping up to the front lines to protect his community.
For nine years, Mike has balanced a dual purpose: driving innovation at Motorola Solutions by day and serving as a fully warranted volunteer officer with the Warwickshire Police Special Constabulary by night. His dedication recently went a step further, as he committed four weeks of his personal time off to complete a rigorous emergency driving course.
As a "Special Constable," Mike wears the same uniform and holds the same authority as a full-time officer. He has logged more than 3,000 hours of service, the equivalent of two full years of police work. His commitment began on his university commute where he watched officers meet chaos with calm. Seeing them guide people through their darkest moments inspired him to move past watching and start helping.
Mike's service ranges from routine patrols to critical, life-or-death interventions. Notably, he recently earned his fourth Chief Constable Commendation after stepping into a major house fire while off-duty. Without hesitation, he ran toward the danger, administered first aid to those trapped inside and helped contain the blaze.
In recognition of his 3,000 hours of service and recent act of bravery, Mike was honored with the 2025 CEO Award for Volunteerism, Motorola Solutions' highest award for service.

Motorola Solutions expects broad-based growth, projecting 2026 gains of 10%–11% in mission-critical networks, about 11% in video security and about 15% in command-center software, supported by modernization of public-safety and federal infrastructure.

Motorola Solutions (NYSE:MSI) is focused on executing across its mission-critical networks, command center software and video security businesses while scaling its recently acquired Silvus Technologies and D-Fend Solutions operations, Chief Operating Officer Jack Molloy said at a Truist conference.
Molloy described Motorola Solutions as a provider of public-safety, enterprise-security and defense-security solutions. The company's strategy centers on an "ecosystem" that combines voice, data, video and command-center software to support incident response and security operations for public agencies, defense organizations and critical-infrastructure customers.

Silvus Capacity Expansion and Defense Demand
Molloy said Silvus, acquired in August 2025, is expected to generate about $850 million in 2026 sales based on current capacity. Motorola Solutions has added a production line in Culver City, California, and expects a Salt Lake City facility to begin contributing in the first quarter of 2027.
He said the Salt Lake City operation is modular and can support additional investment in manufacturing lines. Motorola Solutions has also more than doubled Silvus' sales force, expanded research and development investment and broadened international coverage.
Silvus provides mobile ad hoc network, or MANET, technology designed for operations in congested and contested environments. Molloy said demand is being supported by defense modernization efforts in the U.S., NATO countries and the Indo-Pacific region, as well as investments in unmanned systems.
While the company sees opportunities for Silvus in public safety during temporary events such as the Super Bowl and presidential inaugurations, Molloy said the current commercial focus remains on defense because spectrum is not broadly allocated for Silvus' public-safety uses.

The company sees its D-Series infrastructure refresh cycle as a five- to seven-year opportunity. On costs, Molloy said rising DRAM and flash-memory prices have most affected the video business. He said the company has maintained comparable gross margins and delivered 170 basis points of operating-margin expansion this year.
Looking ahead, Molloy said his priorities are maintaining growth across the core businesses and ensuring Silvus and D-Fend have the resources to scale. He said the company remains acquisitive, with its capital-allocation framework directing 60% toward mergers and acquisitions and share repurchases, 30% toward dividends and 10% toward operating expenses.

Motorola Boosts Counter-Drone Security Footprint With D-Fend Buyout
Motorola Solutions, Inc. MSI has augmented its presence in the rapidly expanding counter-drone security market with the acquisition of D-Fend Solutions. The transaction adds D-Fend's field-proven counter-unmanned aerial systems (C-UAS) technology to Motorola's broader mission-critical safety and security ecosystem.
The $1.5-billion deal appears to be the call of the hour as unauthorized drones increasingly pose security risks to airports, stadiums, critical infrastructure, military installations and densely populated areas. In addition to securing another fast-growing business, D-Fend expands Motorola's addressable market, enabling it to leverage extensive public-safety customer relationships to accelerate adoption of counter-drone technology.
D-Fend Strengthens Counter-Drone Capabilities
The D-Fend acquisition is expected to strengthen Motorola's presence in the fast-growing counter-drone market. D-Fend's EnforceAir platform differentiates itself from conventional systems that typically rely on jamming or kinetic interception, which can disrupt nearby communications or pose collateral risks.
EnforceAir uses radio-frequency cyber-takeover technology to detect and assume control of unauthorized drones and safely redirect them to a designated landing area. Importantly, the platform can neutralize rogue drones without affecting authorized drone operations or surrounding communications infrastructure. This makes the solution well suited for sensitive environments such as airports, large public events, urban areas and other locations where jamming or kinetic methods may be less practical.
Acquisition Bolsters Broader Drone Strategy
The buyout also complements Motorola's expanding presence across the unmanned-systems ecosystem. Through Silvus Technologies, the company already offers resilient wireless networking solutions used in defense applications, including unmanned platforms. Its partnership with BRINC further provides public-safety agencies with drones-as-first-responders capabilities, enabling aerial situational awareness and real-time video transmission to command centers.
The addition of D-Fend broadens Motorola's exposure across defense-focused unmanned communications, public-safety drone applications and counter-drone solutions. Moreover, the company's established relationships with federal agencies, state and local public-safety organizations and enterprise customers could provide a ready distribution channel for D-Fend's offerings.
Management noted that Motorola has worked with D-Fend for several years and jointly pursued opportunities with federal law-enforcement agencies prior to the transaction. The combination of complementary technologies and an established customer network could support D-Fend's growth without requiring Motorola to build a separate go-to-market infrastructure.
Despite the $1.5-billion purchase price and related financing costs, management expects the transaction to be modestly accretive to earnings in 2027. D-Fend's existing profitability, healthy growth trajectory and expanding addressable market are likely to support the expected contribution.
The buyout could eventually produce a more comprehensive air-to-ground security platform, offering a product breadth that may become increasingly important as public-safety customers look to consolidate security workflows rather than deploy isolated point solutions. It could further help Motorola better compete with rivals such as Ondas Inc. ONDS, Unusual Machines, Inc. UMAC and Draganfly Inc. DPRO.

Young America Capital Advises DeepNeuronic on Sale to Motorola Solutions
Tue, September 29, 2026 at 8:22 AM PDT 2 min read
Covilhã-based AI video analytics company to be integrated into Motorola Solutions' Avigilon platform
MAMARONECK, N.Y., Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Young America Capital, LLC ("YAC") today announced that it advised DeepNeuronic, a Portuguese developer of AI video analytics, on its sale to Motorola Solutions, Inc. (NYSE: MSI). Motorola Solutions acquired 100% of DeepNeuronic's share capital, including its Brazilian subsidiary. Terms were not disclosed.
DeepNeuronic was founded in 2021 by Vasco Lopes and Bruno Degardin, who met at Portugal's University of Beira Interior and earned their PhDs there in artificial intelligence and computer vision. Their software reads live camera feeds and flags incidents as they happen. Highway operators, airports, manufacturers and retailers in Portugal and Brazil already run it on the cameras they have. Motorola Solutions will build the technology into Avigilon, its video security platform, which serves customers in more than 100 countries. DeepNeuronic's 17-person team is joining Motorola Solutions and will stay in Covilhã.
"This was one of the sharper deals we worked on this year," said Peter Formanek, Founder and CEO of YAC. "Vasco and Bruno had a product customers were already paying for and a clear view of where video analytics was going. Motorola Solutions saw it too. Our job was to get both sides to a deal that worked, across two continents and a lot of time zones, and Ran did exactly that."
Ran Zfoni, Vice President and Head of Israel & Europe Tech at YAC, advised DeepNeuronic's founders through the transaction. Cuatrecasas served as legal counsel to DeepNeuronic, with a team led by partner Vasco Bivar de Azevedo.
"The founders knew what they wanted: a buyer that could scale the technology and would keep the team together in Covilhã," said Zfoni. "Motorola Solutions was that buyer. Congratulations to Vasco, Bruno and everyone at DeepNeuronic."
Young America Capital, LLC is an investment bank based in Mamaroneck, New York. YAC advises founders and owners of lower-middle-market companies in the U.S. and abroad on M&A, capital raising and strategic transactions. Member FINRA/SIPC. www.yacapital.com

Motorolans on a Mission: Serving the Community From the Office to the Front Lines
Tue, September 29, 2026 at 6:35 AM PDT 3 min read
NORTHAMPTON, MA / ACCESS Newswire / September 29, 2026 / While most people use their vacation to disconnect, U.K.-based Motorola Solutions employee Mike Beddoes dedicates his time to answering a higher call, stepping up to the front lines to protect his community.
For nine years, Mike has balanced a dual purpose: driving innovation at Motorola Solutions by day and serving as a fully warranted volunteer officer with the Warwickshire Police Special Constabulary by night. His dedication recently went a step further, as he committed four weeks of his personal time off to complete a rigorous emergency driving course.
As a "Special Constable," Mike wears the same uniform and holds the same authority as a full-time officer. He has logged more than 3,000 hours of service, the equivalent of two full years of police work. His commitment began on his university commute where he watched officers meet chaos with calm. Seeing them guide people through their darkest moments inspired him to move past watching and start helping.
Mike's service ranges from routine patrols to critical, life-or-death interventions. Notably, he recently earned his fourth Chief Constable Commendation after stepping into a major house fire while off-duty. Without hesitation, he ran toward the danger, administered first aid to those trapped inside and helped contain the blaze.
In recognition of his 3,000 hours of service and recent act of bravery, Mike was honored with the 2025 CEO Award for Volunteerism, Motorola Solutions' highest award for service.
"Receiving this type of recognition is an incredible honor," said Mike. "But the real reward is the impact we get to make on the ground. When you're responding to an emergency or stepping into a critical situation, you aren't thinking about the hours or the personal time off you gave up - you're just focusing on the person who needs your help. I'm grateful to be in a position to protect and serve the community I live in."
Mike serves as a vital bridge between the technologies Motorola Solutions delivers and the first responders who rely on them. His front-line experience gives him a uniquely powerful perspective. When Mike holds a radio in the middle of an emergency, he knows exactly what's at stake. He understands firsthand that a clear signal and a reliable device are more than convenient features - they're critical lifelines. Mike brings this profound connection to our purpose back to his daily work at Motorola Solutions, inspiring his team to build with the end-user in mind.
Mike's journey is a powerful reminder that our impact extends beyond our technology. It's measured in the lives we touch and the communities we help keep safe. He stands alongside Motorolans around the world who embody this same spirit and a shared dedication to serve.

Motorola (MSI) Has Cash to Deploy. Where Can it Create the Most Value?
Mon, September 28, 2026 at 2:19 PM PDT 3 min read
On September 9, Motorola Solutions, Inc. (NYSE:MSI) announced that its Board of Directors approved a $2 billion expansion to its share repurchase program, raising the company's cumulative repurchase authorization since July 2011 to $20 billion. The updated program has no fixed expiration date and builds on the company's previously authorized $18 billion buyback plan, which had approximately $0.6 billion in remaining capacity at the end of Q2 2026. Under the program, management retains flexibility to repurchase shares periodically through open-market or privately negotiated transactions based on prevailing market conditions.

Motorola Solutions, Inc. (MSI) Has Cash to Put to Work. Where Could It Create the Most Value?
Capital Authorization Directly Supported by Cash Flow
For Motorola Solutions, Inc. (NYSE:MSI), expanding share repurchase capacity reinforces management's confidence in the company's long-term earnings trajectory and cash generation capability. In Q2 2026, the company generated $469 million in operating cash flow, up $197 million year-over-year, and $414 million in free cash flow. High cash conversion of reported profitability provides the necessary liquidity to execute open-market repurchases without compromising operational liquidity or dividend payments.
Furthermore, broad-based operational strength supports ongoing capital allocation. Q2 2026 revenue rose 13% year-over-year to $3.1 billion, driven by 15% growth in Products and Systems Integration ($1.91 billion) and 10% growth in Software and Services ($1.23 billion). Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 330 basis points to 32.9%, while non-GAAP EPS grew 24% to $4.41. Multi-year revenue visibility is further underpinned by a record ending backlog of $15.6 billion (up 11%), providing a predictable multi-quarter revenue foundation that reduces reliance on short-term procurement cycles.
Capital Allocation Trade-offs and Balance Sheet Risks
While buybacks enhance per-share metrics, dedicating capital to share repurchases presents strategic trade-offs given the company's leverage profile and capital requirements. A debt-heavy balance sheet increases sensitivity to interest expenses and macroeconomic shifts, making large capital returns dependent on uninterrupted cash flow generation.
Additionally, capital directed toward share buybacks must compete with near-term operational cost pressures and strategic acquisitions. Higher memory and component costs are projected to weigh on second-half gross margins, requiring sustained productivity gains. At the same time, Motorola Solutions, Inc. (NYSE:MSI) agreed to acquire counter-drone technology firm D-Fend Solutions for $1.5 billion in Q2 2026, introducing integration expenses that could temporarily pressure profitability and management capacity while combining operations.

The $2 billion increase in share buyback authorization reflects a shareholder-friendly strategy backed by strong Q2 2026 cash flow and record contract backlog. However, investors must evaluate whether aggressive stock repurchases remain the most efficient use of capital relative to debt reduction, managing elevated component cost headwinds, and successfully integrating new acquisitions like D-Fend Solutions.

Louisiana public safety contract adds to revenue pipeline

According to Zacks, Motorola Solutions shares trade at 25.49 times forward earnings versus 30.95 times for the broader wireless equipment industry, while the stock has declined 1.7% over the past year against the industry’s 23.4% gain, highlighting both underperformance and potential catch-up room if contract-driven growth feeds through to earnings.

Motorola Solutions last reported quarterly results for the most recent interim period within the past nine months, giving investors an anchor for today’s valuation as management highlighted double-digit revenue growth in mission-critical communications and video security, alongside expanding operating margins in that report.

Since March 2026, Motorola Solutions has been in a holding pattern, floating around $456.35. The stock also fell short of the S&P 500's 18% gain during that period.
Given the weaker price action, is now a good time to buy MSI? Or should investors expect a bumpy road ahead? Find out in our full research report, it's free.
Why Is Motorola Solutions a Good Business?
Born from the company that invented the first portable handheld police radio in 1940, Motorola Solutions (NYSE:MSI) provides mission-critical communications, video security, and command center software solutions for public safety agencies and enterprise customers.
1. Skyrocketing Revenue Shows Strong Momentum
Examining a company's long-term performance can provide clues about its quality. Any business can experience short-term success, but top-performing ones enjoy sustained growth for years. Over the last five years, Motorola Solutions grew its sales at an impressive 9.2% compounded annual growth rate. Its growth surpassed the average business services company and shows its offerings resonate with customers.
2. Adjusted Operating Margin Rising, Profits Up
Adjusted operating margin is one of the best measures of profitability because it tells us how much money a company takes home after subtracting all core expenses, like marketing and R&D. It also removes various one-time costs to paint a better picture of normalized profits.
Looking at the trend in its profitability, Motorola Solutions's adjusted operating margin rose by 6.4 percentage points over the last five years, as its sales growth gave it immense operating leverage. Its adjusted operating margin for the trailing 12 months was 31.2%.

3. Excellent Free Cash Flow Margin Boosts Reinvestment Potential
If you've followed StockStory for a while, you know we emphasize free cash flow. Why, you ask? We believe that in the end, cash is king, and you can't use accounting profits to pay the bills.
Motorola Solutions has shown terrific cash profitability, enabling it to reinvest, return capital to investors, and stay ahead of the competition while maintaining an ample cushion. The company's free cash flow margin was among the best in the business services sector, averaging 18.9% over the last five years.

Motorola Solutions (NYSE:MSI) secured a long term statewide public safety technology contract with Louisiana covering multiple agencies.
The agreement expands Louisiana's existing land mobile radio network partnership to include body cameras, evidence management tools and smart radios.
New features in the rollout include real time situational awareness platforms and language translation capabilities for frontline personnel.
The Louisiana public safety contract reshapes how the state buys mission critical tech, which lines up with broader trends our research tracks. We have also spotted 2 warning signs worth knowing about at Motorola Solutions.

The Louisiana award is a US$139 million, 10 year commitment that runs across mobile video, digital evidence, command center software and radio infrastructure. This agreement lines up closely with the existing Narrative, which highlights multi year infrastructure refresh cycles like D Series upgrades and the shift toward software and services. A Closer Look at the Upcoming Payout and Long-Term Dividend Strength
Motorola Solutions Inc (NYSE:MSI) recently announced a total dividend of $1.21 per share, with the ex-dividend date set for 2026-09-16. This includes a cash dividend of $1.21 per share payable on 2026-10-15. For income-focused investors, the ex-dividend date is a critical marker: shareholders must own the stock before this date to qualify for the payment. As investors look forward to this upcoming distribution, the spotlight also shines on the company's dividend history, yield, and growth rates. Using data from GuruFocus, let's look into Motorola Solutions Inc's dividend performance and assess its sustainability.

Motorola Solutions Inc is a leading provider of communications and analytics, primarily serving public safety departments as well as schools, hospitals, and businesses. The bulk of the firm's revenue comes from sales of land mobile radios and radio network infrastructure, but the firm also sells surveillance equipment, dispatch software, and other networking capabilities. Most of Motorola's revenue comes from government agencies, while roughly 25% comes from schools and private businesses. Motorola has customers in over 100 countries and in every state in the United States. This diversified, mission-critical customer base provides a durable revenue foundation that supports the company's consistent capital return program.

A Glimpse at Motorola Solutions Inc's Dividend History
Motorola Solutions Inc has maintained a consistent dividend payment record since 2011, with dividends currently distributed on a quarterly basis. More importantly, the company has increased its dividend each year since 2011. The stock is thus listed as a dividend achiever, an honor given to companies that have raised their dividend each year for at least the past 15 years. This track record reflects management's disciplined commitment to returning capital to shareholders, even through varying economic cycles. For value investors, such consistency often signals financial strength and a shareholder-friendly capital allocation strategy.
Below is a chart showing annual Dividends Per Share for tracking historical trends.
Motorola Solutions Inc's Dividend Analysis · us.finance.gurufocus
Breaking Down Motorola Solutions Inc's Dividend Yield and Growth
As of today, Motorola Solutions Inc currently has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 1.00% and a 12-month forward dividend yield of 1.02%. The slightly higher forward yield suggests an expectation of increased dividend payments over the next 12 months. While a yield near 1% may appear modest compared to some high-yield sectors, it is important to weigh it against the company's rapid dividend growth and strong share price appreciation, which together have delivered substantial total returns for long-term holders.
Over the past three years, Motorola Solutions Inc's annual dividend growth rate was 11.30%. Extended to a five-year horizon, this rate stayed the same. And over the past decade, Motorola Solutions Inc's annual dividends per share growth rate stands at an impressive 11.60%. This double-digit growth cadence means investors who purchased shares years ago now enjoy a far higher effective yield on their original investment than the current headline yield implies.
Based on Motorola Solutions Inc's dividend yield and five-year growth rate, the 5-year yield on cost of Motorola Solutions Inc stock as of today is approximately 1.71%. Yield on cost measures the annual dividend return relative to an investor's original purchase price, assuming reinvested dividends and historical growth. It illustrates how a steadily rising dividend can compound an investor's income stream over time, even when the current yield looks unremarkable.
Motorola Solutions Inc's Dividend Analysis · us.finance.gurufocus
The Sustainability Question: Payout Ratio and Profitability
To assess the sustainability of the dividend, one needs to evaluate the company's payout ratio. The dividend payout ratio provides insights into the portion of earnings the company distributes as dividends. A lower ratio suggests that the company retains a significant part of its earnings, thereby ensuring the availability of funds for future growth and unexpected downturns. As of 2026-06-30, Motorola Solutions Inc's dividend payout ratio is 0.29, meaning the company pays out only about 29 cents of every dollar earned. This conservative ratio leaves ample room for continued dividend increases and reinvestment in the business.
Motorola Solutions Inc's profitability rank offers an understanding of the company's earnings prowess relative to its peers. GuruFocus ranks Motorola Solutions Inc's profitability 9 out of 10 as of 2026-06-30, suggesting good profitability prospects. The company has reported net profit in 9 years out of the past 10 years. Strong and consistent profitability is the bedrock of a reliable dividend, and Motorola's track record here reinforces confidence in its ability to sustain and grow future payouts.
To ensure the sustainability of dividends, a company must have robust growth metrics. Motorola Solutions Inc's growth rank of 9 out of 10 suggests that the company's growth trajectory is good relative to its competitors. A high growth rank indicates that the business is expanding its revenue, earnings, and operating cash flow at a healthy pace, which in turn supports the capacity to raise dividends without straining the balance sheet.
Revenue is the lifeblood of any company, and Motorola Solutions Inc's revenue per share, combined with the 3-year revenue growth rate, indicates a strong revenue model. Motorola Solutions Inc's revenue has increased by approximately 9.30% per year on average, a rate that outperforms approximately 74.29% of global competitors. This top-line expansion reflects steady demand for the company's communications and analytics solutions across its government and commercial customer base.
The company's 3-year EPS growth rate showcases its capability to grow its earnings, a critical component for sustaining dividends in the long run. During the past three years, Motorola Solutions Inc's earnings increased by approximately 14.10% per year on average, a rate that outperforms approximately 66.77% of global competitors. Earnings growth that outpaces dividend growth helps keep the payout ratio stable or declining over time.
Lastly, the company's 5-year EBITDA growth rate of 19.20% outperforms approximately 73.32% of global competitors. EBITDA, or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, is a widely used measure of operating profitability. This strong five-year trend underscores Motorola's ability to convert revenue growth into cash earnings, which ultimately funds both reinvestment and shareholder returns.
Motorola Solutions Inc presents a compelling profile for dividend-focused value investors. The upcoming $1.21 per share payment, payable on 2026-10-15 to shareholders of record before the 2026-09-16 ex-dividend date, continues a streak of annual dividend increases dating back to 2011. With a payout ratio of just 0.29, a profitability rank of 9 out of 10, and double-digit growth in revenue, EPS, and EBITDA, the dividend appears well supported by the underlying business. The modest headline yield of roughly 1% is offset by an 11.60% ten-year dividend growth rate, which has steadily lifted the yield on cost for long-term holders. Investors seeking a growing income stream alongside capital appreciation may find the stock worth monitoring.

Motorola Solutions Eyes Defense, Drone Security Growth as Silvus Scales
Interested in Motorola Solutions, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.
Motorola Solutions expects broad-based growth, projecting 2026 gains of 10%–11% in mission-critical networks, about 11% in video security and about 15% in command-center software, supported by modernization of public-safety and federal infrastructure.
Silvus Technologies is becoming a major defense growth driver, with approximately $850 million in expected 2026 sales at current capacity. Motorola is expanding production, sales and R&D as demand grows for secure communications in contested environments and unmanned-systems operations.
D-Fend Solutions expands Motorola's counter-drone opportunity in public safety, airports, critical infrastructure and venues. The business was selected for a $1.5 billion U.S. Department of Homeland Security grant program and uses cyber-based technology to take control of and safely land threatening drones.
Motorola Solutions (NYSE:MSI) is focused on executing across its mission-critical networks, command center software and video security businesses while scaling its recently acquired Silvus Technologies and D-Fend Solutions operations, Chief Operating Officer Jack Molloy said at a Truist conference.
Molloy described Motorola Solutions as a provider of public-safety, enterprise-security and defense-security solutions. The company's strategy centers on an "ecosystem" that combines voice, data, video and command-center software to support incident response and security operations for public agencies, defense organizations and critical-infrastructure customers.

"We're focused on our end-user markets, providing outcomes that bring together not just the mission-critical network solution, which was fundamentally the bedrock of our company, but the command center software, as well as video," Molloy said.
Molloy said the company has seen public-safety technology budgets grow faster than overall public-safety and state budgets. While some municipalities face fiscal pressure, he characterized Motorola Solutions' offerings as necessary rather than discretionary, citing investments in next-generation 911 systems, network refreshes and public-safety communications devices.

AXON: Competition Intensifies as Motorola Makes $4.4B Acquisition
He also pointed to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act as a multiyear tailwind for the company's federal business, saying U.S. government agencies have older fleets of devices and infrastructure that need modernization.
The COO said Motorola Solutions reported record second-quarter orders and double-digit order growth in the first half of the year. The company has guided for double-digit product growth in the second half. Molloy cited the following growth expectations for 2026:
Mission-critical networks growth of 10% to 11%.
Video security growth of about 11%.
Command center software growth of about 15%.
→ The AI Bottleneck Is Not Chips Anymore and 3 Pipeline Stocks Are Cashing In
Command center software growth includes roughly $100 million in APX NEXT applications expected by the end of fiscal 2026, according to Molloy. Those applications are designed to extend radio-network capabilities with functions including location information and programming that can reduce tasks previously requiring weeks to complete.
Silvus Capacity Expansion and Defense Demand
Molloy said Silvus, acquired in August 2025, is expected to generate about $850 million in 2026 sales based on current capacity. Motorola Solutions has added a production line in Culver City, California, and expects a Salt Lake City facility to begin contributing in the first quarter of 2027.
He said the Salt Lake City operation is modular and can support additional investment in manufacturing lines. Motorola Solutions has also more than doubled Silvus' sales force, expanded research and development investment and broadened international coverage.
Silvus provides mobile ad hoc network, or MANET, technology designed for operations in congested and contested environments. Molloy said demand is being supported by defense modernization efforts in the U.S., NATO countries and the Indo-Pacific region, as well as investments in unmanned systems.
While the company sees opportunities for Silvus in public safety during temporary events such as the Super Bowl and presidential inaugurations, Molloy said the current commercial focus remains on defense because spectrum is not broadly allocated for Silvus' public-safety uses.
He said the company views the Silvus opportunity as durable even if individual conflicts change, arguing that the technology is supported by longer-term military modernization needs and both long-cycle programs of record and near-term operational requirements.
D-Fend Targets Counter-Drone Security Market
Motorola Solutions also recently completed its acquisition of D-Fend Solutions, which provides cyber-based counter-drone technology. Molloy said D-Fend will operate as a separate business and will focus on public-safety end markets including cities, airports, critical infrastructure and entertainment venues.
He said D-Fend systems were deployed at 11 of 12 FIFA sites and at the U.S. Open. The company intends to use Motorola Solutions' North American and international public-safety sales relationships to expand D-Fend's reach.
Molloy said D-Fend was the only cyber-mitigation counter-unmanned aircraft system vendor selected in a U.S. Department of Homeland Security counter-drone grant program totaling $1.5 billion. He said D-Fend's technology can detect and mitigate drone threats by taking control of and landing drones rather than destroying them in the air.
Network Refreshes, Video Wins and Cost Management
The company sees its D-Series infrastructure refresh cycle as a five- to seven-year opportunity. Motorola Solutions supports 40 statewide U.S. networks, 10 Canadian provincial networks and approximately 1,300 underlying P25 networks, Molloy said. Customers are considering upgrades for improved channel efficiency, lower power consumption and greater network resiliency.
Molloy also cited recent competitive wins in video security, including business with the Florida state patrol, Kansas City and Louisiana Highway Patrol. The Louisiana deal includes body-worn and in-car video as well as a P25 network refresh. He said the company is winning business through its integrated product ecosystem, total cost of ownership and AI-enabled workflow tools such as translation, transcription and digital evidence management.
On costs, Molloy said rising DRAM and flash-memory prices have most affected the video business. Motorola Solutions has responded by accelerating inventory purchases, working with suppliers to secure supply continuity and implementing three "substantial" video price increases. He said the company has maintained comparable gross margins and delivered 170 basis points of operating-margin expansion this year.
Looking ahead, Molloy said his priorities are maintaining growth across the core businesses and ensuring Silvus and D-Fend have the resources to scale. He said the company remains acquisitive, with its capital-allocation framework directing 60% toward mergers and acquisitions and share repurchases, 30% toward dividends and 10% toward operating expenses.
Motorola Solutions, Inc develops mission-critical communications and technology solutions for public safety organizations, government agencies and commercial enterprises. Its offerings include land mobile radio systems, broadband communications, command-center software, computer-aided dispatch, records management, evidence management and emergency call-handling technologies.
The company also provides video security and access-control solutions, including body-worn cameras, in-car video systems, fixed video surveillance and related analytics.

Motorola Solutions Announces Increase to Share Repurchase Program
CHICAGO — September 9, 2026 — Motorola Solutions, Inc. (NYSE: MSI) today announced that its board of directors has approved a $2 billion
increase to the share repurchase program, raising the total authorization since July 2011 to $20 billion, with no expiration date for the program. Under the company’s previously authorized $18 billion share repurchase program,
approximately $0.6 billion in repurchase authority remained at the end of the second quarter of 2026. The company may continue to repurchase shares from time to time in the open market or in other privately negotiated transactions, subject to
market conditions.
About Motorola Solutions | Solving for safer
Safety and security are at the heart of everything we do at Motorola Solutions. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and
places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Learn more about our commitment to innovating for a safer future for us all
at www.motorolasolutions.com.

Flex Unveils Axiom As Its AI Infrastructure Spin-Off
Flex Ltd. (NASDAQ:FLEX) on Tuesday unveiled Axiom Solutions International Inc. as the name of its planned independent cloud and power infrastructure company. The move advances Flex's plan to separate the fast-growing business into a standalone public company.
Flex also filed a preliminary Form 10 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Following the planned spin-off, Axiom is expected to trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker AXM.
Axiom will combine power, thermal management and computing systems. The business aims to address growing infrastructure demands from artificial intelligence and data centers.
Flex expects to complete the separation in the first quarter of 2027. However, the transaction remains subject to several conditions. These include final board approval, effectiveness of the Form 10, shareholder approval and Singapore High Court approval.
Separately, Flex said Amy B. Schwetz will join the company on Oct. 5 as chief financial officer of its Regulated Manufacturing Services and Integrated Technology Services segments. She is expected to become Flex CFO after the separation.
Schwetz has more than 25 years of finance and accounting experience. She previously served as CFO of Flowserve Corp. and Peabody Energy Corp.
Flex also outlined the expected boards of both companies. The appointments include George R. Oliver and Brian Yoor at Flex, as well as Mark Eubanks and David Johnson at Axiom.

FLEX Makes a $4.4 Billion Bet on AI Power
Flex Ltd. (NASDAQ:FLEX) announced on September 3 that it will acquire power conversion systems maker ​EPC Power in a deal valued at $4.4 ‌billion. The strategic move will increase the contract manufacturer's exposure to the rapidly growing market for electricity infrastructure serving artificial intelligence data centers.
The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, after which EPC ​Power will become part of Flex's Cloud and Power Infrastructure (CPI) ‌segment. The company expects to finance the ​acquisition through a combination ​of debt ⁠and equity, with committed financing provided by Citi and Bank of America.
Revathi Advaithi, CEO of Flex, stated:
"A generational shift in power architecture is underway, driven by rising power density and the changing demands of digital infrastructure. EPC Power brings leading power conversion and grid-forming technology that positions us to capitalize on this shift, delivering 800V power conversion today and building towards solid-state transformers. Together with our existing power, cooling and compute capabilities, this transaction expands our ability to design and deliver digital infrastructure as an integrated system."

EPC Power Adds New Growth Engines:
EPC Power serves data centers, utility-scale energy storage, and microgrids, giving Flex additional avenues to capitalize on the soaring demand for power infrastructure beyond the AI sector.
Moreover, the acquisition is particularly significant because Flex intends to spin off its CPI business into a standalone public company in the first quarter of 2027. EPC Power's technologies will help Flex benefit from the shift to next-generation power systems and broaden the portfolio of the planned standalone company.
The financial benefits of the deal are also important. EPC Power is expected to generate around $800 million of revenue in 2026, with organic revenue growth of approximately 40% expected in 2027. At the same time, the company's EBITDA margin is also projected to expand by double-digit percentage points to approximately 30% next year.
A Costly Bet for Flex:
The $4.4 billion price tag puts substantial pressure on Flex's balance sheet, and the transaction must generate sufficient incremental earnings and cash flows to justify the valuation. Additionally, the contract manufacturer will need to integrate the acquired technology and operations while also preparing CPI to operate as an independent entity. Any delays or problems in the integration could complicate the spin-off process.
There are also growing concerns of a potential AI bubble. Hyperscalers may be committing to data center investments at a scale and pace that could prove difficult to justify if the economic returns from those projects fall behind expectations. If AI spending is eventually cut back or slowed down, it could significantly weaken the expected growth in power demand.
Conclusion:
Flex's $4.4 billion acquisition of EPC Power expands its exposure to the rapidly growing power infrastructure market and supports its planned spin-off of the CPI business. However, the deal's valuation, integration risks, and a potential pullback in AI data center spending could create challenges and limit upside.

Flex Unveils Axiom As Its AI Infrastructure Spin-Off
Flex Ltd. (NASDAQ:FLEX) on Tuesday unveiled Axiom Solutions International Inc. as the name of its planned independent cloud and power infrastructure company. The move advances Flex's plan to separate the fast-growing business into a standalone public company.
Flex also filed a preliminary Form 10 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Following the planned spin-off, Axiom is expected to trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker AXM.
Axiom will combine power, thermal management and computing systems. The business aims to address growing infrastructure demands from artificial intelligence and data centers.
Flex expects to complete the separation in the first quarter of 2027. However, the transaction remains subject to several conditions. These include final board approval, effectiveness of the Form 10, shareholder approval and Singapore High Court approval.
Separately, Flex said Amy B. Schwetz will join the company on Oct. 5 as chief financial officer of its Regulated Manufacturing Services and Integrated Technology Services segments. She is expected to become Flex CFO after the separation.
Schwetz has more than 25 years of finance and accounting experience. She previously served as CFO of Flowserve Corp. and Peabody Energy Corp.
Flex also outlined the expected boards of both companies. The appointments include George R. Oliver and Brian Yoor at Flex, as well as Mark Eubanks and David Johnson at Axiom.
Stock Performance And Technical Analysis
Flex stock is trading slightly lower Tuesday as risk appetite remains weak across equities. The Nasdaq is down 0.53%, while the S&P 500 has shed 0.48%. Technology stocks are also modestly lower.
The stock is also in a technically sensitive area after pulling back from recent highs. That could put nearby support levels in focus if market weakness continues.
It remains in a longer-term uptrend despite its recent pullback. The stock is 11.9% above its 200-day simple moving average. However, it is 2.5% below its 20-day SMA and 8.9% below its 50-day SMA.
The 20-day SMA is below the 50-day SMA, signaling near-term weakness. However, the 50-day SMA remains above the 200-day SMA. That keeps the longer-term trend constructive.
Momentum may also be improving. The MACD is above its signal line, while the histogram is positive. That suggests selling pressure is easing.
Key resistance sits near $116, followed by the 50-day SMA at $118.43. Support is near $105. A break below that level could put the 200-day SMA in focus.

The Motorola Razr Flex, scheduled for release in December 2026, is poised to challenge the dominance of premium foldable phones, such as Samsung’s Z Fold 8. By focusing on affordability and strategic compromises, Motorola aims to make foldable technology more accessible to a broader audience. This bold move could reshape the mid-range foldable segment, compelling competitors to rethink their pricing and design strategies. The video below from Techtics gives us more details about the rumored foldable.
Watch this video on YouTube.
Who is the Razr Flex Designed For?
Unlike high-end foldable devices that cater to luxury buyers, the Razr Flex is tailored for consumers seeking innovative technology without the hefty price tag. With a price point under $1,500, it significantly undercuts the $1,900 Samsung Z Fold 8, making it an attractive option for users who have been hesitant to invest in foldable devices due to cost. This pricing strategy positions the Razr Flex as a practical choice for tech enthusiasts and everyday users alike, bridging the gap between premium features and affordability.
Design: A Balance of Style and Practicality
The Razr Flex features a “passport-style” foldable design, prioritizing both functionality and aesthetics. When folded, its 5-inch cover display offers a compact, smartphone-like experience, ideal for quick tasks and portability. Once unfolded, the 7-inch inner screen provides ample space for multitasking, gaming and media consumption, rivaling the usability of a small tablet. While it is slightly bulkier than the Z Fold 8, the Razr Flex remains lighter than other flagship devices, such as the iPhone Duo. This thoughtful design strikes a balance between portability and functionality, making it a versatile choice for users who value convenience without compromising on screen real estate.
To maintain its competitive price, Motorola has equipped the Razr Flex with a slightly less powerful Snapdragon processor. While it may not match the performance of top-tier chips, it is more than capable of handling everyday tasks, including casual gaming, productivity apps and media streaming. This calculated trade-off ensures a smooth and reliable user experience without inflating the device’s cost. For most users, the performance of the Razr Flex will be more than sufficient for their daily needs, offering a balance of power and affordability.
The Razr Flex features an impressive camera setup, featuring dual 50MP rear cameras and dual 32MP selfie cameras. This configuration allows users to capture high-quality photos and videos, whether it’s detailed landscapes or vibrant selfies. The camera system is designed to deliver near-flagship performance, making it a strong contender in its price range. For photography enthusiasts, the Razr Flex offers a versatile and reliable option, making sure that users can document their experiences with clarity and precision.
Battery Life and Charging: Designed for Convenience
Equipped with a 5,000mAh battery, the Razr Flex is built to last through a full day of typical use. It supports full-speed wireless charging and magnetic charging, offering flexibility and convenience for users who are constantly on the move. These features enhance the device’s practicality, making sure that users can stay connected without the frustration of frequent recharging. The combination of long battery life and versatile charging options makes the Razr Flex a dependable choice for those who prioritize convenience.
Motorola has made deliberate compromises to achieve the Razr Flex’s competitive pricing. While the device is slightly thicker and less powerful than premium models like the Z Fold 8, these trade-offs are carefully balanced by its affordability and well-rounded feature set. The engineering behind the Razr Flex ensures that users still enjoy a high-quality experience, with features that cater to both practicality and performance. By focusing on what matters most to everyday users, Motorola has created a device that delivers value without unnecessary extravagance.
The introduction of the Razr Flex has the potential to disrupt the foldable phone market. By offering a mid-range device with premium-like features, Motorola is challenging competitors like Samsung to reconsider their pricing strategies and product offerings. This move could ignite increased competition, driving innovation and ultimately benefiting consumers by expanding their options. The Razr Flex demonstrates that foldable technology can be both accessible and functional, setting a new benchmark for the mid-range segment.
The Motorola Razr Flex represents a significant step forward in making foldable phones more accessible to a wider audience. With its innovative design, competitive pricing, and practical features, it offers a compelling alternative to premium models like the Samsung Z Fold 8. By addressing the cost barrier, Motorola is not only broadening its audience but also redefining expectations for mid-range foldable devices. Whether you’re a tech enthusiast looking for innovative features or a budget-conscious buyer seeking value, the Razr Flex is a device that deserves attention.

Flex Announces New Company Name for the Planned Cloud and Power Infrastructure Spin-Off and Files Form 10 Registration Statement
AUSTIN, Texas, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Flex (Nasdaq: FLEX) today unveiled Axiom Solutions International, Inc. (Axiom) as the name of its planned independent Cloud and Power Infrastructure company and filed its preliminary Form 10 registration statement (Form 10) with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), marking a key milestone in the planned spin-off from Flex (Spin-Off). Following completion of the planned Spin-Off, Axiom is expected to trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "AXM."
The Form 10 provides additional information about Axiom, including its business, strategy, financial profile, leadership team and the anticipated terms of the separation.
"Axiom is built to lead the next generation of critical digital and electrical infrastructure," said Revathi Advaithi, Flex Chief Executive Officer and expected Chief Executive Officer of Axiom. "By bringing together power, thermal management and compute at the system level, we help customers deploy increasingly complex infrastructure with greater speed and scale, as AI drives new demands on the physical infrastructure behind it."
The name Axiom reflects a foundational principle: bringing together power, cooling and compute at the system level to support the reliable, scalable infrastructure needed for the future.
The planned separation is expected to be completed in the first quarter of calendar 2027, subject to customary conditions, including, among other things, final approval by the Flex Board of Directors, the effectiveness of the Form 10 and Flex shareholder and Singapore High Court approval.
Upon completion, Flex and Axiom are expected to operate as independent publicly traded companies. Additional details on each company's strategy will be shared at Innovation Day on November 10, 2026, in Austin, Texas.
For additional information about Axiom visit axiomsolutions.com
Flex (Reg. No. 199002645H) is the manufacturing partner of choice that helps leading brands design, build, and manage products that improve the world. With a global footprint spanning 30 countries, Flex delivers advanced manufacturing and supply chain solutions, innovative products and technology, and lifecycle services that support customers from concept to scale. In the AI era, Flex is helping customers accelerate data center deployment by solving power, heat, and scale challenges through cutting-edge power and cooling technology and scalable IT infrastructure solutions. For information about Flex's intent to spin off its Cloud and Power Infrastructure portfolio, visit: https://flex.com/transaction-resources.

FLEX Makes a $4.4 Billion Bet on AI Power
Flex Ltd. (NASDAQ:FLEX) announced on September 3 that it will acquire power conversion systems maker ​EPC Power in a deal valued at $4.4 ‌billion. The strategic move will increase the contract manufacturer's exposure to the rapidly growing market for electricity infrastructure serving artificial intelligence data centers.
The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, after which EPC ​Power will become part of Flex's Cloud and Power Infrastructure (CPI) ‌segment. The company expects to finance the ​acquisition through a combination ​of debt ⁠and equity, with committed financing provided by Citi and Bank of America.
Revathi Advaithi, CEO of Flex, stated:
"A generational shift in power architecture is underway, driven by rising power density and the changing demands of digital infrastructure. EPC Power brings leading power conversion and grid-forming technology that positions us to capitalize on this shift, delivering 800V power conversion today and building towards solid-state transformers. Together with our existing power, cooling and compute capabilities, this transaction expands our ability to design and deliver digital infrastructure as an integrated system."
Arista (ANET) Has $13.3 Billion of Cash and No Debt at All. What Is That Worth?
EPC Power Adds New Growth Engines:
EPC Power serves data centers, utility-scale energy storage, and microgrids, giving Flex additional avenues to capitalize on the soaring demand for power infrastructure beyond the AI sector.
Moreover, the acquisition is particularly significant because Flex intends to spin off its CPI business into a standalone public company in the first quarter of 2027. EPC Power's technologies will help Flex benefit from the shift to next-generation power systems and broaden the portfolio of the planned standalone company.
The financial benefits of the deal are also important. EPC Power is expected to generate around $800 million of revenue in 2026, with organic revenue growth of approximately 40% expected in 2027. At the same time, the company's EBITDA margin is also projected to expand by double-digit percentage points to approximately 30% next year.
A Costly Bet for Flex:
The $4.4 billion price tag puts substantial pressure on Flex's balance sheet, and the transaction must generate sufficient incremental earnings and cash flows to justify the valuation. Additionally, the contract manufacturer will need to integrate the acquired technology and operations while also preparing CPI to operate as an independent entity. Any delays or problems in the integration could complicate the spin-off process.
There are also growing concerns of a potential AI bubble. Hyperscalers may be committing to data center investments at a scale and pace that could prove difficult to justify if the economic returns from those projects fall behind expectations. If AI spending is eventually cut back or slowed down, it could significantly weaken the expected growth in power demand.
Conclusion:
Flex's $4.4 billion acquisition of EPC Power expands its exposure to the rapidly growing power infrastructure market and supports its planned spin-off of the CPI business. However, the deal's valuation, integration risks, and a potential pullback in AI data center spending could create challenges and limit upside.

Tue, September 29, 2026 at 6:08 AM PDT 4 min read
Tariffs that can reach 100% on goods from key Russian oil buyers are not just a headline. They reshape where factories sit, which suppliers matter, and how resilient your portfolio really is. Supply chains that once leaned heavily on distant hubs may shift closer to U.S. shores. In this article you will see three U.S. onshoring and nearshoring stocks that appear positioned to benefit, and how this new rulebook could affect your next move.
The three stocks below are just a sample from this theme, and the full screen surfaced 65 more manufacturers and assemblers with equally compelling reshoring narratives that are not covered here. To go wider and identify your own highest conviction ideas, head straight to the U.S. onshoring and nearshoring manufacturers screener to filter, analyze, and focus your shortlist.
Overview: Hammond Power Solutions designs and builds transformers across Canada, the U.S., Mexico, and India for grids, industry, infrastructure, and EV charging. This anchors it firmly in the North American nearshoring theme.
Operations: Hammond Power Solutions generates about CA$1.06b from transformer manufacturing and sales, with roughly CA$806 million from the U.S. and Mexico and CA$222 million from Canada.
Hammond Power Solutions gives this onshoring theme real-world wiring, with a transformer footprint already rooted in North American factories and now gearing up for a bigger role in regional power infrastructure.
"The ramp-up of new manufacturing facilities in Mexico, with expectations to be fully loaded and operational by early next year, will significantly increase production capacity, positioning Hammond to capture greater share of increasing North American demand and support long-term revenue growth while enabling improved operating leverage and margin expansion."
What happens to Hammond Power Solutions' future margins and pricing power depends heavily on how one unseen cost pressure ultimately resolves.
Those margin pressures sit at the center of the full narrative for Hammond Power Solutions, where capacity, pricing power, and hidden cost risks all collide in one accelerating reshoring story.
TSX:HPS.A Revenue & Expenses Breakdown as at Sep 2026
Overview: Flex runs large scale contract manufacturing and design for electronics, automotive, healthcare, and industrial customers, with major onshoring ready facilities across the U.S. and Mexico that plug directly into the reshoring theme.
Operations: Flex generates about US$7.2b from Cloud and Power Infrastructure, US$11.6b from Integrated Technology Solutions, and US$10.5b from Regulated Manufacturing Solutions, with substantial revenue coming from Mexico, the U.S., China, and other global hubs.
Flex matters for this reshoring screen because it does not just assemble products, it gives global brands a ready made way to pull production closer to U.S. customers when tariff risk flares up.
"Flex can offer hyperscalers and Fortune 500 enterprises true "nearshoring," building complex hardware in Mexico for US markets or in Eastern Europe for EU markets."
What happens to Flex's margins and growth now largely turns on how one concentrated stream of high value AI hardware demand evolves.
That AI hardware surge is only the start, and the full narrative for Flex lays out how Flex could leverage nearshoring scale and pricing power, as well as any risks that might be masking beneath it.
NasdaqGS:FLEX Revenue & Expenses Breakdown as at Sep 2026
Overview: Array Technologies manufactures utility scale solar tracking systems and control software, supplying hardware that helps U.S. projects support the onshoring clean energy buildout.
Operations: Array Technologies generates about US$1.10b from Array Legacy Operations and roughly US$82 million from STI Operations, primarily tied to solar tracking products.
Array Technologies matters for this reshoring theme because its tracking systems are built to sit inside U.S. and nearshore solar farms rather than depend on imported Chinese hardware.
"First, whether Array actually pays the preferred dividend in cash now that the five-year deferral option has expired, if the annual burden stabilizes near $32 million, that is a constructive sign. If the company instead starts letting dividends accrue at the penalty rate, the senior claim is not just expensive anymore, it is growing. Second, how efficiently that $2.5 billion order book actually converts into shipped revenue and free cash flow. A backlog is a promise, not a delivered result, and the gap between the two is where a discount of this size either gets confirmed or quietly closes."
What happens when one pressure quietly shifts inside that order book could influence how much of the domestic solar buildout ultimately reaches shareholders.
When that pressure inside the backlog starts to shift, the full narrative for Array Technologies shows where Array Technologies could still turn today's constraints into accelerating domestic solar leverage.

Can Flex Maintain Its Advanced Networking Momentum in FY27?
Mon, September 28, 2026 at 6:01 AM PDT 4 min read
Flex Ltd. FLEX is seeing continued strength in its communications business, with advanced networking identified as one of the company's high-value growth markets. On the last earnings call, management stated that the business is expected to drive growth over a sustained period, supported by pull-through demand from data centers. Communications remain one of the largest businesses within Flex's post-separation portfolio, with advanced networking spanning high-speed switches, optical switches and network interface cards.
The advanced networking business has contributed to Flex's recent performance. On the last earnings call, management highlighted that it was a significant driver of the company's fiscal fourth- and first-quarter results, with its strength expected to continue into the fiscal second quarter and fiscal 2027. The company is seeing increased demand from customers it has worked with for several years, while also winning share in certain product segments. The business has exposure across a number of large original equipment manufacturers and multiple product categories, including high-speed switching, optical products and interface technologies.
Flex also highlighted the diversity of its advanced networking business across both customers and product segments. Management stated this combination of sustained customer demand, customer diversity and product diversity supports the continued strength of the business. The company expects communications to remain an important part of its business following the planned separation of its Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment.
Looking ahead, management expressed confidence in the durability of advanced networking into fiscal 2028, linking the business to continued AI infrastructure spending. As data center demand continues, Flex expects the advanced networking business to continue to ramp alongside that spending. The company's focus on high-value growth markets is also part of its strategy for the business following the separation.
Overall, Flex's comments indicate that advanced networking is expected to remain a sustained growth market within its communications business, supported by data center demand and broad exposure across customers and networking technologies.
Sanmina Corporation SANM continues to benefit from expanding cloud and AI infrastructure demand, supported by its vertically integrated manufacturing model and broader systems capabilities following the ZT Systems acquisition. New accelerated compute programs and deeper customer relationships improve revenue visibility and support growth beyond the current fiscal year. A diversified end-market mix and healthy liquidity provide flexibility to fund capacity and future programs. Favorable business mix and disciplined execution also support earnings growth. Fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 revenues are expected to be in the range of $3.3-$3.6 billion. The company also raised its fiscal 2026 outlook, expecting revenue of $14-$14.3 billion, up from the previous $13.7-$14.3 billion range.
Plexus Corp. PLXS is benefiting from increasing program ramps. It recorded 31 manufacturing wins totaling $255 million of annualized revenue in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, driven by the Industrial and Aerospace and Defense market sectors. The funnel of qualified manufacturing opportunities is $4.5 billion, indicating a strong growth pipeline. Strategic investments in capacity and emerging areas like data centers strengthen growth prospects. Fiscal fourth-quarter revenues are projected between $1.33 billion and $1.38 billion. At the midpoint, the revenue outlook implies a 4% sequential rise and 28% year-over-year growth. Management now expects fiscal 2026 revenue growth above 20% and adjusted operating margin greater than 6%. Plexus expects fiscal 2027 revenue growth to exceed the 9-12% goal, alongside further margin expansion.
Flex Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates
Shares of FLEX have gained 99.2% in the past year compared with the Electronics - Miscellaneous Products industry's growth of 45%.
FLEX trades at a forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 22.05, below the industry's 29.14.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for FLEX's fiscal 2027 earnings has been revised upward over the past 60 days.
FLEX currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Flex also filed a preliminary Form 10 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Following the planned spin-off, Axiom is expected to trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker AXM.
Axiom will combine power, thermal management and computing systems. The business aims to address growing infrastructure demands from artificial intelligence and data centers.
Flex expects to complete the separation in the first quarter of 2027. However, the transaction remains subject to several conditions. These include final board approval, effectiveness of the Form 10, shareholder approval and Singapore High Court approval.
Separately, Flex said Amy B. Schwetz will join the company on Oct. 5 as chief financial officer of its Regulated Manufacturing Services and Integrated Technology Services segments. She is expected to become Flex CFO after the separation.
Schwetz has more than 25 years of finance and accounting experience. She previously served as CFO of Flowserve Corp. and Peabody Energy Corp.
Flex also outlined the expected boards of both companies. The appointments include George R. Oliver and Brian Yoor at Flex, as well as Mark Eubanks and David Johnson at Axiom.
Stock Performance And Technical Analysis
Flex stock is trading slightly lower Tuesday as risk appetite remains weak across equities. The Nasdaq is down 0.53%, while the S&P 500 has shed 0.48%. Technology stocks are also modestly lower.
The stock is also in a technically sensitive area after pulling back from recent highs. That could put nearby support levels in focus if market weakness continues.
It remains in a longer-term uptrend despite its recent pullback. The stock is 11.9% above its 200-day simple moving average. However, it is 2.5% below its 20-day SMA and 8.9% below its 50-day SMA.

APH's AI Connectivity Growth Accelerates: Can It Outpace TEL & MRVL?
Mon, September 28, 2026 at 7:22 AM PDT 4 min read
Amphenol APH is benefiting from strong order momentum, improving operating leverage and robust profitability, strengthening its position across artificial intelligence (AI) data-center, communications and industrial connectivity markets. In the second quarter of 2026, orders grew 94% year over year and 14% sequentially to $10.7 billion, resulting in a book-to-bill ratio of 1.23:1. Every end market recorded a positive book-to-bill ratio, highlighting broad-based demand and improving revenue visibility. This momentum enhances APH's competitive positioning against Marvell Technology MRVL and TE Connectivity TEL.
Higher sales are also driving meaningful operating leverage. The adjusted operating margin expanded 420 basis points year over year and 250 basis points sequentially to 29.8%. Even excluding tariff recoveries, the margin approached 29%. CommScope contributed more than $1.2 billion in second-quarter sales and operated at a margin above 20%, including acquisition-related amortization. Management attributed the improvement to better factory execution, vendor management, SG&A discipline and leverage from higher volumes. Amphenol also raised its expected 2026 CommScope revenues to $4.6 billion from $4.1 billion, and doubled expected adjusted EPS accretion to 30 cents from 15 cents.
AI infrastructure remains a key growth driver. IT datacom represented 43% of second-quarter sales, with revenues rising 89% year over year and 63% organically. Sequential sales increased 22%, with virtually all growth driven by AI-related products. Amphenol is benefiting from demand for high-speed copper, fiber-optic and power interconnects, while CommScope is expanding its advanced optical presence. Strong execution is translating into higher earnings and cash flow. Adjusted EPS rose 67% year over year to $1.35, while operating and free cash flows reached $1.6 billion and $1.2 billion, respectively. APH ended the quarter with $8.4 billion of liquidity and a net leverage ratio of 1.3 times, supporting capacity expansion, product development and acquisitions.
Marvell Technology is challenging APH through rapid AI data-center growth and improving operating leverage. MRVL's second-quarter fiscal 2027 results raised the revenue outlook to roughly $12 billion, implying 45% growth, and lifted its fiscal 2028 revenue outlook to $18 billion, representing nearly 50% growth. Data-center revenues are expected to rise 60% in fiscal 2027 and more than 60% in fiscal 2028, driven by strength across interconnect, switching and custom businesses. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, the non-GAAP operating margin was 36.6%, up 180 basis points year over year, demonstrating significant operating leverage in the business.
TE Connectivity is also pressuring APH through record orders and stronger profitability. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, the company reported record orders of $5.7 billion, up 27% year over year, while Digital Data Networks orders increased more than 70% from the start of the fiscal year to the end of the third quarter. Investors might want to bet on TE Connectivity (TEL), as it has been recently upgraded to a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). This upgrade is essentially a reflection of an upward trend in earnings estimates -- one of the most powerful forces impacting stock prices.
The Zacks rating relies solely on a company's changing earnings picture. It tracks EPS estimates for the current and following years from the sell-side analysts covering the stock through a consensus measure -- the Zacks Consensus Estimate.
Since a changing earnings picture is a powerful factor influencing near-term stock price movements, the Zacks rating system is very useful for individual investors. They may find it difficult to make decisions based on rating upgrades by Wall Street analysts, as these are mostly driven by subjective factors that are hard to see and measure in real time.
As such, the Zacks rating upgrade for TE Connectivity is essentially a positive comment on its earnings outlook that could have a favorable impact on its stock price.
Most Powerful Force Impacting Stock Prices
The change in a company's future earnings potential, as reflected in earnings estimate revisions, and the near-term price movement of its stock are proven to be strongly correlated. That's partly because of the influence of institutional investors that use earnings and earnings estimates for calculating the fair value of a company's shares. An increase or decrease in earnings estimates in their valuation models simply results in higher or lower fair value for a stock, and institutional investors typically buy or sell it. Their transaction of large amounts of shares then leads to price movement for the stock.
For TE Connectivity, rising earnings estimates and the consequent rating upgrade fundamentally mean an improvement in the company's underlying business. And investors' appreciation of this improving business trend should push the stock higher.

Amphenol APH is benefiting significantly from accelerating demand in the IT datacom market, particularly for artificial intelligence (AI)-related applications. In the second quarter of 2026, IT datacom represented 43% of APH's total sales, with revenues surging 89% year over year and 63% organically.
